findings.message: resolveRepoPhases treats a read that has no entry for a phase as 'the phase is gone' and drops the stored entry. Only a missing `read` keeps the stored phases. But phaseTimesOf (sync/specclaw.ts and the bundled plugin copy) always returns an object. It is `{}` when state.json is missing, and it leaves out any phase whose status is no longer the 'reached' value. A phase whose status has moved on, and a sender that couldn't read the phase at all, both come out as 'not there', so a recorded repo phase is deleted from meta.repoPhases. Its history line disappears and its `repo:<phase>` pin stops resolving. The README says phase times a sender didn't read keep the stored ones. Fix: merge per phase. Keep each stored entry the read doesn't give, unless the design says a phase can be un-reached; in that case say so and test it.
findings.scenario: FLT-301 has repoPhases.verify = {at: 2026-10-07, source: main@…} stored, and a chat message pins `repo:verify`. A later review round sets state.json's verify.status to 'pending' (or state.json is missing on that read). The next push sends phaseTimes {proposal: …} with no verify, and resolveRepoPhases returns {proposal} only. 'Verified in the repo' is removed from the history, and get_proposal_event(line: 'repo:verify') now fails for the pinned record.

findings.message: repoLines reads the stored phases through normalise(), which returns null when any entry fails the schema. One malformed entry in meta.repoPhases (for example an old row, or a hand edit) hides every repo history line, with nothing on screen to say they couldn't be read. Fix: parse each entry on its own and drop or flag only the bad one, or surface an 'unreadable' marker.
findings.scenario: meta.repoPhases = {proposal: {at: '2026-10-01T05:00:00Z', source: 'main@abc'}, verify: 'garbage'} → the history shows no repo lines at all, not even 'Approved in the repo'.

findings.message: For sync_proposal, the read that each new phase entry records as its source is `input.meta.source`. That is caller-supplied text that is never checked against the commit-sha rule (sync/sha.ts). The history line then shows it as 'From the repo, read at <text>'. The final-pass comment says the source is 'never the caller's word', but on this path it is. Fix: validate meta.source as `<ref>@<sha>` (SHA_RE) in SyncInput before it can be stored as a phase's pinned read, or store null there.
findings.scenario: sync_proposal with meta: {source: 'release-candidate', repoPhases: {verify: '2026-10-07T10:00:00Z'}} → the history line reads 'Verified in the repo · From the repo, read at release-candidate', which names no commit.
